response.markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: strengthen competition within one GRU4Rec model using a multi-negative ranking objective.** At 0% research progress, an objective-only intervention offers a practical first experiment; improvements remain unmeasured.

**Insights from the starting point.**

1. Module checks pass across all four categories. Generated-predictor parity remains unverified, so serialization checks alone cannot establish deployment consistency.
2. Electronics has weaker sampled training separation than CDs_and_Vinyl: negative-beats-positive rates are 0.0768 versus 0.0058. These measurements motivate investigating discrimination but do not establish validation performance.
3. Latest-item deletion increases sampled target rank by 3.64–6.98 positions, versus 0.48–0.70 for oldest-item deletion. This demonstrates temporal reliance, without identifying current user intent or justifying stronger recency bias.

**Insights from related work.**

1. Krichene and Rendle show that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons [1]. Consequently, diagnostic margins cannot substitute for the pinned benchmark.
2. Prakash et al. report popularity-dependent effects of negative sampling [2]. More competitive training should therefore retain head/middle/tail diagnostics rather than assume uniform benefits.
3. ExUA attributes sequential-recommendation uncertainty to historical interactions [3]. Attribution could localize reliance, but it supplies neither missing compatibility labels nor evidence that changing reliance improves accuracy.

These insights organize three directions: deployment correctness, training competition, and temporal attribution. Their common framework is:

| Direction | Observable evidence | Minimal intervention | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|---|
| Correctness | Module checks pass | Check generated predictor | Does routing preserve scores? |
| Competition | Weak sampled margins | Multi-negative objective | Does validation HR@10 improve? |
| Temporal reliance | Matched perturbations | Lag-matched attribution tests | Which dependencies generalize? |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality / future potential / code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform multi-negative objective [1,2] | 3 / 7 / 3 | Established machinery; directly increases training competition | More compute; unobserved competitors may be relevant |
| Popularity-balanced negative sampling [2] | 3 / 6 / 4 | Tests head/tail discrimination explicitly | Can sacrifice aggregate accuracy |
| Lag-matched attribution interventions [3] | 4 / 6 / 6 | Tests explanations within the same network | Diagnostic value need not translate into gains |

**Selected experiment.** Preserve the corrected GRU4Rec backbone and replace its ranking loss with cross-entropy over one positive and 64 unique uniform negatives. For each supervised prefix, exclude padding, its observed items and the target from negative eligibility; retain the positive once. Use all eligible negatives when fewer than 64 exist. Compute the loss in FP32 and average positions within each sequence before averaging sequences.

```text
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
for each valid aligned prefix and target:
    negatives = unique_uniform(eligible_training_items, 64)
    logits = predict_score(features_at_position, [target] + negatives)
    loss_for_position = logsumexp(logits) - logits[0]
backpropagate(mean_per_sequence(loss_for_position))
```

Keep architecture, optimizer and other hyperparameters fixed to isolate the objective. Retain one checkpoint per category, all routing, seeds 0/42, 200 batches/epoch and at most 200 epochs. Preserve diagnostic interfaces and use the final nonpadding position for inference. Verify the generated predictor against that checkpoint; select solely through unchanged macro validation HR@10 within the shared budget.

idea.description: Replace the corrected GRU4Rec baseline's ranking objective with cross-entropy over one positive and up to 64 unique uniformly sampled negative items at each valid supervised position. Train exactly one independent GRU4Rec model per category, preserving the supplied backbone, routing and inference score function.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics show weaker positive-negative training separation in Electronics and demonstrate that temporal dependencies already affect predictions. Increasing simultaneous competition is a focused first hypothesis that avoids assuming the model needs stronger recency bias. Neither the diagnostic margins nor the user feedback establishes that this intervention will improve validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only supplied training interactions. At each supervised timestep, construct exclusions from that timestep's observed prefix, the positive target and reserved IDs; never consult validation or test interactions for sampling. Draw up to 64 distinct negatives uniformly without replacement from eligible real training-catalog items. Include the target exactly once, including repeated targets; exclude invalid input/target positions. If no negatives are eligible, skip the position and report the count. Compute logsumexp in FP32 with temperature 1 and no additional auxiliary objective. Average valid position losses within each sequence, then average sequences with valid supervision. This weighting is part of the declared experiment; report it explicitly when comparing against the supplied baseline. Keep the corrected architecture, optimizer, regularization and other hyperparameters fixed. Chunk candidate scoring if needed to bound GPU memory; do not change the 200 batches per epoch or maximum 200 epochs. Sampling must use a dedicated deterministic training RNG seeded 42 so diagnostic execution cannot alter training draws. Preserve preprocessing seed 0. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView hooks. Keep log2feats output aligned to original left-padded positions, use fresh recurrent state per independent history, and gather the maximum nonzero index for inference. Architecture and inference scores are unchanged by this loss; nevertheless, verify generated working/predict.py routing and checkpoint-loaded scores against the trained module using the same single checkpoint per category. Keep unavailable metadata breakdowns empty with explanations. Training margins remain descriptive; do not treat embedding concentration as recommendation diversity or perturbation sensitivity as current intent. Host macro validation HR@10 is the only selection metric. No trained auxiliary predictors, score fusion, checkpoint averaging, external data or hidden-test access. Account for added sampling, scoring and diagnostics within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.
idea.pseudocode:
def multi_negative_loss(view, sequence, positive, rng):
    # Existing corrected GRU4Rec; features preserve B x L alignment.
    features = view.log2feats(sequence)
    sequence_losses = []
    for b in range(sequence.shape[0]):
        prefix = set()
        position_losses = []
        for t in range(sequence.shape[1]):
            item = int(sequence[b, t])
            if item == 0:
                continue
            prefix.add(item)
            target = int(positive[b, t])
            if target == 0:
                continue
            excluded = prefix | {target} | reserved_ids
            negatives = sample_unique_uniform(
                training_catalog_ids, excluded, max_count=64, rng=rng)
            if len(negatives) == 0:
                record_skip('no_eligible_negatives')
                continue
            candidates = tensor([target] + negatives, device=features.device)
            logits = view.predict_score(features[b, t], candidates).float()
            position_losses.append(logsumexp(logits, dim=-1) - logits[0])
        if position_losses:
            sequence_losses.append(stack(position_losses).mean())
    return stack(sequence_losses).mean() if sequence_losses else None

# Vectorize/chunk candidate generation and scoring in the implementation.
# Keep baseline model and optimizer; use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42.
# Train one model/category, 200 batches/epoch, at most 200 epochs.
# Preserve diagnostic APIs and writer; verify actual generated-predictor parity.
# Inference: gather features at max index where sequence != 0, never count-1.
# Select using only the unchanged host macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Connects measured GRU4Rec separation limitations to a narrowly specified competition experiment with explicit eligibility and sequence weighting.
originality.negative: Multi-negative cross-entropy is established; the supplied evidence supports an experiment rather than a novel algorithmic contribution.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled starting point for studying how competition strength affects category and popularity strata within a fixed recurrent family.
future_potential.negative: Additional negatives may produce diminishing returns or suppress relevant unobserved items; benchmark gains are unverified.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes the training objective while retaining model architecture, scoring hooks and checkpoint format.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient unique sampling with prefix-specific exclusions and bounded candidate-scoring memory requires care and increases training cost.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes how sampled recommendation metrics can differ from full-catalog metrics and change model comparisons.
Supports distinguishing training diagnostics from the task's fixed validation selection metric.
limitations: Does not establish that increasing training negatives improves this GRU4Rec benchmark.
Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. — supplied study on negative sampling and popularity disparities in sequential recommendation
contributions: The supplied research summary reports head/middle/tail disparities under different negative sampling strategies.
Motivates reporting popularity strata alongside aggregate validation accuracy.
limitations: Reported balance improvements can involve aggregate accuracy costs.
The supplied summary does not validate the proposed 64-negative objective on these four datasets.

related_work.title: Explainable Uncertainty Attribution for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses gradient saliency to attribute recommendation uncertainty to historical interactions.
Motivates temporal attribution as a separate diagnostic research direction.
limitations: Attribution does not establish causal user intent or supply unavailable compatibility and ownership labels.
Does not directly support a validation improvement from the selected objective.
